entries.definition: A quick current-strength number: the rounded average of the player's seven stored attributes. Open the player file to see the individual stats and their caps.

The total attribute points normal training can still add before the player's seven Archetype caps. It is the sum of each cap minus the current attribute, with above-cap attributes counting as zero remaining. A larger number means more development headroom, and the number falls as the player improves.
The player's development identity. It speeds growth in favored attributes and sets each attribute's training cap. The + and − labels show the strongest and weakest development areas.
Changes career behavior: wage demands, preferred negotiation pitches, patience before requesting a transfer, and likely retirement timing. It does not directly add match stats.

Personal renown earned from playing, results, goals, strong league finishes, and cups. Fame raises renewal demands, adds to club fame, helps unlock stronger coaches, and can qualify a long-serving player as a club legend.
The player's week-to-week physical readiness. Matches and hard Energy Use drain it; rest and recovery restore it. Low condition weakens performance and raises injury risk.
The player's mood. Very low morale reduces effective match stats; repeated low-morale weeks can trigger a transfer request, with patience depending on Personality.
How many seasons the player remains employed. An expired deal must be renewed or the player can leave.
Money paid every week. Improved, famous, greedy, or newly awakened players usually ask for more when their contract is renewed.
The eleven players selected to begin the next match: one goalkeeper and ten outfield players in the active formation.
Running speed and the ability to reach space, support attacks, and recover defensively.
Shot quality and power for outfield players. Goalkeepers store SHO but do not use it as a visible role stat.
Pass selection and execution, especially when pressure or distance makes the ball difficult.
Marking, tackling, interceptions, and resisting attacking actions.
Close control, dribbling, and keeping useful possession in traffic.
How well a player handles physical effort and condition drain across a match.
Goalkeeping reactions and save strength. Outfield players store REF but do not use it as a visible role stat.
The maximum value normal training can reach for one attribute. Caps come from Archetype; a player already above a cap is never reduced.
The players and focus drills trained at weekly settlement. A saved plan repeats until you change it.
A targeted training choice that costs Money and Training Points once per week and gives its listed gains to every assigned player.
The improvement currency. Earn TP through matches and facilities; spend it on focus drills and drill unlocks.
The first required training facility. Building and upgrading facilities improves development and may unlock related systems.
The areas a coach improves. Matching a specialty to a drill or attribute increases training gains over time.
The primary coach, with the strongest specialty bonuses and a weekly wage.
A second, smaller set of specialty bonuses unlocked by building a Coaching Office.
The team's positional shape. Settings holds three presets; the first starts watched matches and the live Formation control cycles them.
Tactical intent: Attack seeks more forward play, Protect values safety, and Balanced sits between them. It is separate from physical effort.
How hard the team works off the ball. Save Energy reduces movement and condition drain; All Out increases movement but drains condition much faster.
A live summary of the on-field team's remaining condition. It helps judge Energy Use and substitutions.
Swap an on-field player for an eligible bench player. Each team has at most three substitutions per match.
Runs the same deterministic match engine instantly with automatic hero timing, substitutions, and Energy Use. Watching can earn an edge through better manual power timing.
A goalkeeper's pressure bar. Saves and power shots damage Resolve, making later saves weaker; it partially recovers at halftime.
A hero's visible, moment-specific super ability. Powers change possession or geometry rather than giving a hidden permanent stat smear.
Momentum earned from touches, tackles, shots, saves, and time on the pitch. Above the threshold, more Heat means a better chance to enter the Zone.
A short glowing activation window. Tap a glowing home hero in Manual mode to fire at full strength before the window fades.
You tap a glowing home hero during the Zone to activate at 100%. A missed window does not auto-fire and leaves half Heat.
The engine fires at the next useful context at reduced strength. Rival heroes and Quick Result always use automatic timing.
The visible delay before a power starts. Many wind-ups can be interrupted, which returns half the hero's Heat.
A permit allowing a powered player to use their power in the next match. You may own more heroes than the number you can license at once.
The hero-progression currency. It comes from power events, first-time hero feats, and season awards, and is spent on power growth and rare Hero Lab actions.
The club-capacity currency used for wages, transfers, facilities, scouting, and events. It is earned from sponsors, tickets, prizes, and player sales.
Supporters who affect home attendance and ticket income. Results, promotions, and memorable heroes can grow the fanbase.
A building placed on club grounds that adds a lasting benefit and usually a weekly upkeep cost.
The recurring weekly Money cost of running a facility.
A bonus discovered when compatible facilities touch on the grounds grid.
A timed search for recruits. Better scouting narrows hidden attribute ranges before you decide whether to negotiate.
The registration period when players may be bought, sold, or listed through the market.
A periodic choice of young prospects. Better youth facilities improve their starting strength.
The five-division league pyramid, from D5 District League to D1 Global League. Strong finishes earn promotion upward.
A knockout competition played alongside the league. Cup progress brings prizes, Fame, and a route to silverware.
Locks in the current management choices and moves the calendar forward to training settlement, events, or match day.
